headline: Bulk Carrier Strikes Delaware River Bridge
subheadline: Bridge allisions keep pilotage in focus
insight: The Singapore-flagged bulk carrier Strategic Alliance struck the open Tacony-Palmyra drawbridge on the Delaware River. No injuries; Coast Guard inspecting the ship.

sources.title: Cargo ship strikes bridge between New Jersey and Philadelphia, causing traffic backup
Singapore-flagged cargo ship strikes US bridge

factCheck.notes: Vessel identity, flag, size, time and mooring location from the U.S. Coast Guard as reported by AP; corroborated by Splash247. Cause not yet established; no investigation findings used.

image.credit: U.S. Navy (Bureau of Ships) / Wikimedia Commons

meta.description: The Singapore-flagged bulk carrier Strategic Alliance (180 m, built 2013) struck the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge over the Delaware River between Philadelphia and Palmyra, New Jersey, at about 1:15 p.m. local time on 12 November 2026, while the drawbridge was open for ship passage. No injuries were reported. The U.S. Coast Guard said the ship is moored at a Kinder Morgan facility in Bristol, Pennsylvania, where a Coast Guard inspection team is on site. The bridge, which carries Route 73 and about 76,200 vehicles a day, reopened that evening with one lane closed; the cause has not been reported.
